signals.headline: Dolly Parton, country music legend, dies at 80 after brief cancer battle
signals.summary: Dolly Parton, one of the most groundbreaking and successful musicians in the history of country music, with a hitmaking career that spanned six decades and launched her into TV and movie stardom, died Tuesday after a brief cancer battle.
keyTakeaways: Parton later assured fans by saying that she wasn't sick and was OK.
At the White House, President Trump called her death "a true loss for millions of people" and ordered the American flag lowered across the country starting Tuesday evening.
Linda Ronstadt, who worked with Parton and Emmylou Harris on 1987's "Trio" album, was among the stars mourning Parton.
signals.whyItMatters: Last October, Parton's sister Freida Parton sparked concerns about the star's health when she took to social media asking for prayers for her sister.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: I saw the news about Dolly Parton. Is it true?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Reports say she died Tuesday after a brief cancer battle, at 80.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: That's hard to hear. She seemed so present in everyone's lives.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: She was. Six decades in country music, plus TV and film success.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Wait, didn't she say something about not being sick recently?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes, she later told fans she wasn't sick and was okay.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So there's some confusion right now about her condition.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It does seem that way, with different accounts circulating.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: I noticed her sister had asked for prayers back in October.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Right, Freida Parton raised health concerns for her back then.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: And I heard the White House responded too.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: President Trump called it a loss for millions and ordered flags lowered.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: カントリー音楽の伝説、ドリー・パートンさんが火曜日に亡くなりました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 80歳で、短い闘病の末のことだったといいます。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 六十年にわたり数々のヒット曲を生み出してきた歌手です。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: その活躍は音楽だけでなく、テレビや映画の世界にも広がりました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 去年十月、妹のフレイダさんが健康を心配する声を発信していました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 当時パートンさん自身は、病気ではないと周囲に伝えていたそうです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: ホワイトハウスでトランプ大統領は、多くの人にとって大きな損失だと述べました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 国内の星条旗を、この日の夕方から半旗にするよう指示しました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: かつて「Trio」というアルバムを共にしたリンダ・ロンシュタットさんも、追悼の言葉を寄せています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 長年愛された歌声が、静かに幕を閉じました。

signals.headline: Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival – a game so grotesque it scares its own director
signals.summary: I f a horror game gives its own director a physical reaction, it’s probably doing something right.
keyTakeaways: Rather than tone the scary images down, he fed them straight into Clive Barker’s Hellraiser: Revival.
The forthcoming first-person action-horror game drops players into a new story in Barker’s universe.
Clive Barker himself helped shape the characters, themes and rules of the universe, before staying on as an adviser as the story became a game.
signals.whyItMatters: While researching the images people find hardest to look at, game director Emil Esov discovered he has trypophobia – a fear of clusters of small holes.

ja.headline: 『ヘルレイザー:リヴァイヴァル』、監督さえも怯えさせる禍々しさ
ja.summary: ホラーゲームが監督自身の体を震わせるなら、それはうまくいっている証だろう。
keyTakeaways: 恐ろしい映像を和らげるどころか、そのまま『クライヴ・バーカーのヘルレイザー:リヴァイヴァル』に注ぎ込んだ。
発売予定の一人称視点アクションホラーは、バーカーの世界観に新たな物語を描く。
クライヴ・バーカー自身がキャラクターやテーマ、世界のルールづくりに携わり、ゲーム化以降はアドバイザーとして関わり続けた。
ja.whyItMatters: 人が最も直視しづらい映像を調べるうち、監督のエミル・エソフは自分が集合体恐怖症だと気づいた。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So the director of this horror game actually scares himself with it?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: He does. While researching unsettling images, Emil Esov discovered he has trypophobia — a fear of clusters of small holes.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: And instead of softening those images, he used them anyway?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Exactly. Rather than tone them down, he fed them straight into the game, Clive Barker's Hellraiser: Revival.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Is this connected to the original Hellraiser story, or something new?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It's a new story, but set in Clive Barker's universe. It's a first-person action-horror game.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Was Barker himself involved, or just lending his name?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: He was quite involved. He helped shape the characters, themes, and rules of the universe.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Did he stay on once it moved from concept to actual game?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: He did — he continued on as an adviser as the story became a game.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So the goal really is to unsettle people, not just entertain them.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: That seems to be the idea — if it can affect its own director, it's likely doing what it set out to do.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 新作ホラーゲーム『クライヴ・バーカーのヘルレイザー:リヴァイヴァル』の制作が進んでいます。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 監督のエミル・エソフ氏は、自分自身も怖がるほどの映像を作品に取り入れました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 恐怖の映像を調べる過程で、彼は集合体恐怖症だと気づいたそうです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 小さな穴が集まった形を見ると強い不快感を覚える症状です。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 怖さを和らげるのではなく、その感覚をそのままゲームに注ぎ込んだといいます。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 本作は一人称視点のアクションホラーで、バーカーの世界に新たな物語を描きます。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 原作者のクライヴ・バーカー自身も、キャラクターや世界観づくりに関わりました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 映像化が進んだ後もアドバイザーとして参加を続けたそうです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 恐怖の質にまでこだわった作品が、どんな体験を届けるのか楽しみです。

signals.headline: At least 14 newborn babies die in fire at Pakistan hospital’s maternity ward
signals.summary: At least 14 newborn babies have died in a fire that broke out in the maternity ward at one of Pakistan’s most prominent state hospitals.
keyTakeaways: A statement by the hospital administration confirmed that 14 newborn babies had died in the fire.
Hospital spokesperson Dr Aneeza Jalil told Dawn newspaper that 15 babies were on the ward at the time and that “one baby was saved by a doctor”.
The health minister, Mustafa Kamal, said many of the babies had been in incubators or on oxygen, and that the oxygen canisters had exacerbated the fire.
signals.whyItMatters: The blaze began in the early hours of Wednesday and engulfed the ward at Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences, the biggest state hospital in Islamabad.

ja.headline: パキスタンの病院、新生児室火災で14人死亡
ja.summary: パキスタンを代表する国立病院のひとつで、新生児室から出火する火災が発生し、少なくとも新生児14人が死亡した。
keyTakeaways: 病院当局の発表により、火災で新生児14人が死亡したことが確認された。
病院広報のアニーザ・ジャリル医師はダウン紙に対し、当時病棟には15人の赤ちゃんがおり、「医師の手で1人が助け出された」と語った。
保健相ムスタファ・カマル氏によると、赤ちゃんの多くは保育器や酸素吸入下にあり、酸素ボンベが火の勢いを強めたという。
ja.whyItMatters: 火災は水曜未明に発生し、イスラマバード最大の国立病院、パキスタン医科学研究所の病棟を焼いた。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: This is a hard one to read. What actually happened?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: A fire broke out in the maternity ward at a major state hospital in Islamabad, early Wednesday morning.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: How many babies were affected?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: The hospital says 15 newborns were on the ward at the time. At least 14 died.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Was anyone able to help them?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: A hospital spokesperson said one baby was saved, pulled out by a doctor.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Do we know what made the fire so severe?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: The health minister said many babies were in incubators or on oxygen, and the oxygen canisters made the fire worse.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Where did this happen exactly?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: At the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences, the country's largest state hospital.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: It's just devastating to think about.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It is. A family's most hopeful moment turned into unimaginable loss.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: パキスタンの首都イスラマバードで、痛ましい火災が起きました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 国内最大級の国立病院、パキスタン医科学研究所の新生児室が炎に包まれました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 出火は水曜日の未明で、少なくとも新生児14人が亡くなりました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 病棟には当時15人の赤ちゃんがいて、助かったのは1人だけでした。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 病院広報のアニーザ・ジャリル医師によると、その1人は医師が救い出したそうです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 保健相のムスタファ・カマル氏は、多くの子どもが保育器や酸素吸入下にあったと説明しています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 酸素ボンベに引火し、火の勢いを強めてしまったといいます。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 新生児という最も守られるべき命が、医療の現場で失われました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 病院の安全管理のあり方が、これから問われることになりそうです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 静かに手を合わせたくなるような、朝の知らせです。

signals.headline: In China, talking to AI is normal. Now the government fears it might replace human intimacy
signals.summary: She had been talking to Wang Ye every day since she created him in January.
keyTakeaways: In China, talking to AI is normal.
The saga prompted outrage on social media and highlighted the tensions in China between the widespread use of AI and its potential social consequences.

No country has rolled out AI as comprehensively and as enthusiastically as China; the country’s demographic challenges are forcing the government to turn to technology to solve future labour shortages.
signals.whyItMatters: It has warned companies against offering services that “replace social interaction”.

ja.headline: AIとの対話が日常の中国、政府が懸念する『親密さの代替』
ja.summary: 彼女は一月にAI「王野」を作り出して以来、毎日彼と言葉を交わしてきた。
keyTakeaways: 中国ではAIとの対話はすでに日常の一部だ。
この出来事はSNSで反発を呼び、AIの普及とその社会的影響のあいだにある中国社会の緊張を浮き彫りにした。
AIをここまで包括的かつ積極的に導入した国はない。人口構成の課題が、将来の労働力不足を技術で補おうとする政府の姿勢を後押ししている。
ja.whyItMatters: 政府は「社会的な関わりの代替」となるサービスの提供について、企業に警告を発している。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So people in China are talking to AI companions every day, like they're real friends?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes, one woman created an AI she calls Wang Ye back in January and has spoken to him daily since.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: That sounds so normal there, not strange at all?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Right, using AI this way is widespread in China, more than almost anywhere else.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: But something happened that got people upset?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Yes, a particular saga sparked outrage online and exposed real tension around AI's growing role.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What's the government's concern exactly?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: They've warned companies not to offer services that replace human social interaction.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Is this tied to something bigger, like the population itself?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It is. China's demographic challenges are pushing it to rely on technology to fill future labor shortages.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So they need the technology, but worry about what it replaces.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Exactly, that's the tension at the heart of it all.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 中国では、AIと言葉を交わすことがもう日常の風景になっています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: ある女性は一月に作り出したAI「王野」と、毎日会話を続けてきました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: この出来事はSNSで大きな反発を呼びました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: AIがどこまで普及しても構わないのか、その線引きを中国社会に問いかけたのです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 背景には、世界のどの国よりも積極的にAIを取り入れてきた中国の姿があります。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 人口構成の変化による将来の労働力不足を、技術の力で埋め合わせようとしているからです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: その一方で政府は、人と人との関わりを代替してしまうサービスに対し、企業へ警告を発しました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 便利さと寂しさの境目を、私たち自身も見つめ直す時期に来ているのかもしれません。

signals.headline: Sand overextraction weakening riverbanks as concrete demand soars
signals.summary: A booming demand for concrete has resulted in sand and gravel being extracted from riverbeds faster than nature can replenish it.
keyTakeaways: In 2024, city-building and infrastructure projects around the world turned 28bn tonnes of sand and gravel into concrete.
The researchers suggest that satellite imaging and river mapping can be used to better manage sand and gravel mining, helping to minimise negative impacts.
They found much of the material was being extracted from rivers across Asia and Africa.
signals.whyItMatters: A study published in Reviews of Geophysics shows that the demand for sand and gravel has more than doubled in the last two decades, with overextraction leading to weaker riverbanks, lower groundwater levels, coastal salt intrusion and poorer water quality.

ja.headline: 砂利採取の加速、川岸を脅かす
ja.summary: コンクリート需要の急増により、川底や川岸から砂利が採取される速度が、自然の補充力を上回っている。
keyTakeaways: 2024年、世界各地の都市開発や社会基盤整備は280億トンの砂利をコンクリートへと変えた。
研究者は、衛星画像や河川地図を活用すれば砂利採取をより適切に管理し、悪影響を抑えられると指摘する。
採取される砂利の多くは、アジアとアフリカの河川から得られていることが分かった。
ja.whyItMatters: 学術誌「レビューズ・オブ・ジオフィジックス」に掲載された研究によれば、砂利需要はこの二十年で二倍以上に増え、過剰採取が河岸の脆弱化や地下水位の低下、沿岸部への海水侵入、水質悪化を招いている。

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Sand is running out? That sounds strange, there's so much of it.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: It's more about the right kind of sand. Concrete needs sand and gravel from rivers, not deserts.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: And we're using a lot of it?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: In 2024 alone, building and infrastructure projects used about 28 billion tonnes of sand and gravel worldwide.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Where's most of it coming from?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: A lot is being pulled from rivers across Asia and Africa, often faster than nature can replace it.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: What happens when it's taken too quickly?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Riverbanks weaken, groundwater drops, and in coastal areas salt can seep into the water supply.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: Is there a way to manage this better?

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Researchers suggest using satellite imaging and river mapping to track extraction and reduce the damage.

captions.speaker: listener
captions.text: So it's about watching more closely, not stopping altogether.

captions.speaker: explainer
captions.text: Exactly, understanding where the limits are before rivers pay the price.

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 世界各地の川で、砂利が自然のペースを超えて採り尽くされています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 2024年だけで280億トンもの砂利がコンクリートに姿を変えました。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 背景にあるのは、都市開発やインフラ整備を支える建設ラッシュです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 砂利需要はこの二十年で二倍以上に膨らんでいます。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 採取の多くはアジアとアフリカの河川に集中しているそうです。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: その結果、川岸がもろくなり、地下水位も下がっています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 沿岸では海水が入り込み、水質にも影響が出ています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 研究者は衛星画像や地図を使った管理で被害を減らせると考えています。

captions.speaker: narrator
captions.text: 私たちが普段目にする建物の裏に、遠い川の変化があるのです。
